title: Rate limiting
proves: Every public route has a measured limit or a written decision (no new unlimited route can merge); the limiter holds under 150 simultaneous requests, recovers after Retry-After, is not dodged by path, header or address-spelling variants or by a forged X-Forwarded-For from an untrusted peer; guessing one account from many networks is stopped without locking the owner out; password-reset mail is capped; every counter expires; and the gate fails on any unresolved Critical or High.
doesNotProve: Behaviour behind a real reverse proxy or CDN (the proxy hop count is a deployment setting this cannot see), production traffic shapes, one-time-code guessing across addresses (the signup flow needs a mail domain that resolves), or authenticated per-user limits on the 1,900 signed-in routes beyond the ones with a declared limit.
